chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Music director for Armstrong; the command performance joke
summary: Armstrong left everything to McRae, including a command performance where he stopped the band on air, joking he wanted McRae's name broadcast.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: What were your duties there? Pretty much as they were with Chick?

I did more there than I did with Chick, because Louie was a different type of man that Chick was, you know. You had to do everything. You had to call all the rehearsals, tell him what time you're gonna leave -- he didn't wanna know. Louie didn't want nothing. He was just -- this was Louie Armstrong and his band. Now, he's got a man that takes care of everything. Even when we did command performances in California and we did all the Coca-cola shows -- rehearsals. You call him just like you call the other musicians. You call a rehearsal, you got to let him know when is rehearsal. He didn't have nothing to do with the music. Like, we had a command performance at -- (inaudible) the Trianon Ballroom where we was playing and told him -- says -- (inaudible). (Inaudible) say, "Look, we come out to see you about the command
performance and the band and so and so." He say, "Well go over and see my music director. I don't have anything to do with that."
"He always take care of everything." These (inaudible) say, "Okay, Mr. Armstrong."

So they came over and talked to me. Say, "Oh, you're the music director." I say, "Yeah." They told me what they wanted. I say, I'll be there at six o'clock -- five o'clock, whenever you want to have rehearsal, have Louie there (inaudible).
He says, "Now we got a big band." Says, "Can I have the arrangement (inaudible)?" (Inaudible). Say, "We'll change that."

So I went out and met the music director -- the Commander (inaudible). And we got together (inaudible) -- straighten out all the parts and things (inaudible) for the big band. Because they had a big string section -- twelve strings.
Five trumpets, four trombones. Five or six rhythm, you know. Great big band.

"You take Louie's band (inaudible)." right of And he walked off the (inaudible) the show (inaudible). Jimmy Durante was the star with a lot of other stars (inaudible). Applause And I walked on. (Inaudible). "Ladies and gentlemen, Louie Armstrong!" The band hit into "Sleepy Time Down South" -- they got a break, you know. This was a two-bar break before Louie comes in, and he started talking -- says, "Hey, take it from the top, Pops ain't got his chops together." And the thirty-two musicians liked to fainted, because that wasn't in the script. I bring my hand down again. And after that, he made the break and went on into it. I say, "Why would you do a foolish thing that?" He say, "So I can get your name on the air."
Coast -- all over the country. This went through all the arm -- overseas, all over -- everywhere. That's what a command performance is. Something that goes all over the country, you know.
